subject: One surgeon, two rooms - the data layer
text:
Hi [NAME],

Yossi's post in February describes the end goal: one surgeon on a complex decompression in Room A, Dynamis executing routine bone milling autonomously in Room B. More patients treated, same surgical workforce.

Getting there means training a new autonomous capability for every new procedure step. Each one needs an annotated operating room video from real cases. That annotation step sits between every completed procedure and every new training run.

The pattern we see at teams your size: the engineers building the models are also manually deciding what to annotate. At 10 cases a month, it is fine, but at 50 it becomes the bottleneck.

We work with Moon Surgical on exactly this & I thought it would be worth a 20-minute call next Thursday afternoon? Let me know.

subject: When the model gets it wrong, the member calls
text:
Hi [NAME],

Your payer customers sell [COMPANY] on member engagement and care gap closure. Both depend on your SLMs getting the recommendation right.

The gap most AI-first teams hit at your scale is knowing whether the model is working before it ships and being able to show that to a payer under HITRUST audit.

We work with Synthesia and Appfolio on that evaluation and curation layer. Teams come to us when model iteration is the priority and building evaluation infrastructure internally is slowing it down.

If relevant, do you have 20 minutes this Thursday to see if there is a parallel?

subject: What ships when the eval loop breaks?
text:
Hi [NAME],

We work with Synthesia and Appfolio on training data curation and model evaluation infrastructure, similar to what the [COMPANY] AI Models team is building for your SLMs and agent chains.

ML leads come to Encord:

• 
Model iteration is blocked by the evaluation layer & not the model itself.

• 
The labelling pipeline design is still owned by ML engineers

• 
HITRUST and payer SLAs make a hallucination a contractual problem

Without these issues fixed:

• 
Agent failures compound before member impact.

• 
Payer audits surface gaps in model output traceability.

If any of that is relevant, let's grab 20 minutes this week and i can show what that setup looks like?

subject: EU AI Act and 9 cardiac indications
text:
Hi [NAME],

the EU AI Act which comes into force in August requires a documented record
of who labelled what for every model update. As i understand, MyCardium
runs 9 indications across two cleared products, which if my math is
correct, is nine separate records to keep current.

The gap is usually the paper trail behind it, which teams struggle with.
We work with abbvie and Conavi Medical team on annotating DICOM series
together for their FDA submission.

Thought it would be relevant to you and am happy to chat further if you're
interested.

subject: Deep Learning Hiring - 1 person 2 jobs
text:
Hi [NAME], 

I saw the Deep Learning Research Engineer role. "Improve our data pipeline" next to "train models" usually means one person doing two jobs?!

We work with teams hitting the same wall, labelling tools built for bounding boxes break down on person-crop embeddings, where identity ambiguity makes every annotation decision harder. 

Automotus had 30,000 images, mostly near-duplicates, no fast way to find them. Embedding-based curation got them to ~10,000, no accuracy loss.

What's eating more of your time right now, models or data pipeline? Would have to chat more if you're free.

subject: line in your ReID post that caught my eye
text:
Hi [NAME],

Saw the two Deep Learning Engineer openings referencing "improve our data pipeline" and "build datasets" alongside model training. Guessing your engineers are still maintaining the labelling infrastructure?

That tends to slow teams down right when they need to move fastest, especially post-Series A. 

Tooling built for one detection task rarely stretches to the next, so every new hire spends part of their ramp rebuilding the pipeline instead of training models.

We saw the same at Automotus. Embedding-based curation cut their 30,000-image dataset to ~10,000 with no accuracy loss, and freed the engineers to get back to model work.

Love the blog, by the way. If you're interested, it would be great to grab 20 minutes to chat later this week?

text:

subject: AgBot T2 Doubling Problem
text:
Hi [NAME], 

We just started working with John Deere on similar autonomous field robot perception use cases as agXeed, so I thought I'd reach out.

Motion engineers in the agricultural robotics space come to us when:

• 

Field incident logs have no automated filter - engineers manually decide which obstacle events are worth pulling into a training dataset.

• 

Annotating LiDAR and camera captures from real field conditions requires a setup that general-purpose tools weren't built for.

• 

The loop from a field failure to a corrected labelled example in the retraining queue takes weeks, not days.

Do you face similar issues at agXeed?

If so, it might be worth having an initial conversation to see whether our offerings fit your needs. I'm free next Wednesday at 2pm.

subject: Vision at Mount Sinai
text:

subject: Less time finding data, more time on models
text:

We work with companies like John Deere on a similar detection workflow. Encord is the curation and annotation infrastructure that sits underneath their image-based defect and quality detection models. 

When their model got a new defect class wrong, they found the right training examples faster because Encord surfaced them automatically instead of engineers hunting through images manually.

With iQS Pro expanding into new geographies and fruit varieties, I thought i'd reach out before the annotation pipeline becomes a bottleneck. 

Do you have 20 minutes next week to compare notes on how you're managing that today?

text:

 Quick one. My team works with Automotus and Flock Safety on camera CV annotation and dataset curation pipelines. 

 I saw the Series A and the push into enterprise security and retail. Expanding into new verticals on top of an existing detection pipeline usually means the labelling infrastructure hasn't caught up. Different environments, different edge cases & different failure modes per detection task.

subject: when eo/ir data meets rf
text:
Hi [NAME],  

 I saw the MoU with Ecliptic Defence and Space, combining electro-optical/infrared and RF sensor data for situational awareness. 

 we work with Forterra on the labelling and QA behind edge-deployed defence perception models. Combining two sensor types usually means combining two labelling standards too, before either model can trust the other's ground truth. 

 pulling two teams worth of training data into one pipeline is the kind of thing that slows your entire engineering team down.  

 I'm curious how that's being scoped? 

 Do you have some time to connect early next week? If so, let me know and ill send over a link.

subject: FDA June Update - every model update needs its own trail
text:
Hi [NAME],

The FDA's June 17 classification for DICOM ML-based radiology devices makes
annotation documentation a legal special control. Combined with CE marking,
eyonis LCS now operates under two parallel post-market documentation
regimes.

The risk: when a regulatory reviewer asks for subgroup-level annotation
evidence behind the last model update, where does that trail live?

We work with Conavi Medical on exactly this: annotation provenance and
audit trail for a regulated imaging AI device.

Is this something you have a process for? Happy to connect this week if
useful.

subject: Data flywheel for L4 autonomy
text:
Hi [NAME] - been following Kakaomobility for some time, and after seeing the recent announcement at COEX around the L4 autonomy roadmap, I thought it would be a great time to get introduced. 

For context, I work on the Physical AI team at Encord, partnering with companies like Woven by Toyota to provide the platform and workforce that scale real-world data pipelines, supporting the journey from L2/L3 to L4 autonomy. We help teams gain greater control over data curation by surfacing the right scenes and edge cases, while enabling frontier use cases such as VLA reasoning and 3D auto-labeling. 

I think there's pieces that could match well with your roadmap. Would you be open to a quick chat later this week? Happy to share what we've learned from supporting other teams on a similar journey.

subject: Point rapide sur Spimed AI
text:
Bonjour [NAME],

[SENDER] de faire ta connaissance. Je travaille avec [SENDER] chez Encord.

Je relisais vos échanges précédents autour des projets de Spimed AI sur
l'analyse de plaque, la dissection aortique et l'embolie pulmonaire.

Je sais qu'à l'époque vous aviez choisi RedBrick, principalement parce que
cela faisait plus de sens commercialement pour la première phase. Je
voulais simplement savoir si les choses avaient évolué depuis, en
particulier sur la labellisation des plaques, les workflows de revue
radiologue ou les besoins de traçabilité FDA.

Nous avons aussi compris que RedBrick commençait à réduire ses opérations,
et nous avons récemment vu plusieurs équipes passer sur Encord en raison
d'une baisse de capacité d'ingénierie et de support de leur côté.

De ce que vous aviez discuté avec [SENDER], la plaque semblait être le sujet
où la qualité d'annotation, le consensus entre reviewers et l'auditabilité
pouvaient devenir plus importants à mesure que le projet avançait.

Je serai à Paris la semaine prochaine avec notre équipe MedTech. Ce serait
super de prendre un café ou un déjeuner si tu as un moment.
